correctness.rationale: Separate the 4 coset compositions of a triple, represent elements as (a,ε) with (a,ε)(b,δ)=(a+(-1)^ε b,ε+δ). For all reflections, inverses agree and Δ=0. For rotations, Δ=0 iff the cyclic exponent triple is a three-term progression, otherwise −1; counting centers and steps gives B=n(n−gcd(n,2))/2−(2n/3)1_(3|n). In mixed cases, direct rotation/reflection components become four-point affine sets whose collision patterns depend on d and t=2a, with separate involution d=n/2 when n even; odd n has t bijective, even n t is twice an even residue. The per-d vectors derived by these cases sum to the exact displayed table and binom(2n,3). Dominant positive mixed sets are n³+O(n²) while all-rotation negative and all-reflection balanced each contribute n³/6+O(n²), yielding limits. Independent raw group multiplication enumerated ALL three-subsets for n=3..21, agreeing in every j and Δ bin. These finite checks corroborate the algebraic all-n proof.

originality.rationale: Ascoli et al (2022), Appendix A, already analyze three-point generalized dihedral sum/product dominance and count aggregate product-dominant subsets in a mixed composition. Their comparison must not be claimed as new. The present theorem refines the aggregate dominance into four exact discrepancy values and counts for every coset type and n mod 4, including balanced and quotient-dominant strata. Amit et al (Oct 2026) prove dihedral product dominance using general probability methods but do not supply this particular fixed-size four-valued table in the inspected stated theorem. The refinement requires additional explicit overlap arithmetic.

value.rationale: A complete exact distribution for the smallest nontrivial subset cardinality of a natural nonabelian group family is a motivated invariant. The four discrepancy types, congruence-dependent counts and limiting proportions sharpen aggregate dominance questions; the exact table can serve as a benchmark for larger-size group-set studies.

final_claim: For every D_n of order 2n, n≥3, every 3-element subset has product–quotient cardinality discrepancy Δ=|AA|−|AA^-1| in {−1,0,1,3}. An exact table for each j∈{0,1,2,3} rotation count and parity of n modulo 4 gives every frequency, and the limiting probabilities of positive, zero, negative discrepancy are 3/4, 1/8, 1/8.
